svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: WDAC REFERENCE POLICY WORKFLOW
svg.desc: One reference PAW builds its App Control policy in six phases. Phases 1 and 2 prepare the device and deploy an audit-mode baseline. Phases 3 and 4 run every needed application, turn the logged 3076 events into allow rules, sanitize them, merge them into the base policy and screen until no new events appear. Phases 5 and 6 turn Audit Mode off, deploy the enforced policy and verify the two STIG findings V-243450 and V-243451. All stages keep one policy GUID with a rising date-based version, apply live with CiTool, and record their evidence.
svg.text: APP CONTROL FOR BUSINESS · AUDIT → MERGE → ENFORCE · ONE POLICY GUID · DATE-BASED VERSIONS · PAW STIG V-243450 / V-243451
C:\WDAC\{Source,Compiled,Events,Logs} · scripts in C:\WDAC-Scripts · every step writes a transcript

g.text: Set up the PAW and load an audit-mode baseline, so Windows starts
0_pre-flight.ps1: folders, transcript, ConfigCI, CI log ≥ 100 MB
Starting STIG recorded (often 2 / 1 on new builds)
[Wizard] Base-Audit.xml: allow Microsoft, Audit Mode, block lists
The Wizard only writes XML. Windows logs no Event 3076 until a compiled
Turn what the apps actually load into allow rules, then prove nothing is
Reboot, then run EVERY app you need (Event 3076)
4_merge…: base FIRST + events SECOND, v2, Y/N, deploy
New 3076 for an app you need? Repeat steps 4 and 5 before you enforce.
Switch the screened policy to enforce and prove both STIG findings
6_enforce_policy.ps1: gate, stamp v3, Y/N, compile, CiTool
Reboot: approved apps run, block-test app blocked (3077)
New-WDACRunReport.ps1: one HTML report of the run
CRITICAL · ONLY AUDIT MODE MAY CHANGE
Script 6 stops if Audit Mode is not the only option turned off, the GUID
changed, or the block-test app is in the policy.

svg.text: One PolicyID GUID · Base-Audit.xml → Base-Audit-Merged.xml → Base-Enforce.xml
Same GUID, rising VersionEx: each stage replaces the last in place (never -ResetPolicyID) · applied live with CiTool
what each stage proves · what keeps the policy safe to change
Microsoft Windows PAW STIG · App Control
Win32_DeviceGuard 0 = OFF · 1 = AUDIT · 2 = ENFORCING · only 2 passes

g.text: Audit stages read user mode 1 (AUDIT): still an open finding
The counter N restarts at 1 each day
Never below the highest known: active, XMLs, archives, GPO packages
Windows replaces a policy only with a HIGHER version
